extractions.description: The paper theoretically and empirically studies combinatorial generalisation in offline reinforcement learning, evaluates DT and RvS on newly collected maze and image-based data, and contributes temporal data augmentation for outcome-conditioned behavioral cloning.

type.quote: Our empirical results support the theory: we demonstrate that prior RL methods based on SL (DT [2] and RvS [3]) fail to perform stitching
type.justification: The paper contains theoretical analysis but also trains and evaluates models in extensive experiments; it is therefore catalogued as empirical.

name.quote: Some reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms can stitch pieces of experience
name.justification: Reinforcement learning is the central field addressed by the paper.

name.quote: Our work focuses on the offline RL setting where the agent has access to a fixed dataset
name.justification: The theory, datasets, and experiments directly address offline RL.

name.quote: Many recent methods view RL as a purely SL problem
name.justification: The paper studies and improves supervised-learning-based sequential decision methods.

name.quote: We formalize this property as a form of generalisation, which we will refer to as combinatorial generalisation.
name.justification: The paper contributes a formal framework and experiments concerning this form of generalisation.
